{"id":"KOD-75","uuid":"1fdb7b23-7dcd-411b-916d-5827bf7fce20","title":"v0.3 L3 — Topology planner + scope walker: blockedBy-graph execution, computed never judged","description":"**Outcome:** A topology planner over the `blockedBy` graph and a walker that dispatches execution-only fires over ready lanes — computed, never judged. Lanes may run concurrently; a lane carries a mark while it is being worked and the walker skips a marked lane (founder ruling 2026-09-09, <issue id="ebb83291-e57e-4be2-87d6-2b69342a0254" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-747/prevent-a-delayed-claim-renewal-from-reclaiming-ownership-after">KOD-747</issue>).
**Measured:** 2026-08-12 — stage-2 validation halted this lane on base resolution, superseded the same day.
**Fix:**

* Planner (`domain/topology.py`): open-blocker predicate, `ScopeCycleError` on a cycle, rank by effective priority then age.
* Walker (`chains/scope_walker.py`): ready-set arithmetic over tracker state, concurrency from configuration with a marked lane skipped, drift reconciliation ticked here, association recorded at dispatch; selection producer generalized.
* Dispatch: plan-time refusal, `scope:approved` per dispatch, the issue itself as target — no marker, no prose parsing; re-entry resumes onto its recorded branch, never a fresh mint.
* Base resolution rides the ready set: trunk when nothing blocks, a blocker's recorded branch, or an integration base for a fan-in; three arms supersede `UnstackableLaneError`.
* The gap, the unit of dispatch: `criterion` sub-issues not Done or Canceled-with-supersession, read lease-free with an owner each; capability check, plateau, residual.
* Walker settings express demonstrated operator choices; stable constants stay with their owning code and capabilities derive from the composed implementation. The configuration contract is owned by <issue id="780387d5-ed58-4987-96dd-ab256be9567d" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-468/kod-75-ac-33-walker-settings-express-operator-choices-stable-constants">KOD-468</issue>, amended under <issue id="a35bb59e-e287-4baa-9ddf-0cc099bfd07c" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-744/architecture-findings-from-the-2026-09-08-v03-review-dead-slices">KOD-744</issue>.

## Accepted v0.3 simplification scope · 2026-09-08

Scheduled under [KOD-744](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-744>). Recheck the earlier counts at the implementation branch.

**Outcome:** Repeated mechanics have one implementation at the layer that owns them, and consumers depend on the port surface they actually use.

**Check / Do:**

* Extract the common bounded backoff mechanics used by the GitHub, Linear and agent-content paths, with a RetryPolicy value (attempts, initial delay, factor, jitter). Preserve each adapter's retryable-error rules, cancellation, timeouts and response handling. Code defaults are permitted; create separate policy instances only for operational differences. <issue id="5c0c178e-6719-4a65-a2d2-fea4a4844e75" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-745/simplify-appconfig-into-subsystem-settings-and-typed-knowledge">KOD-745</issue> consumes these values. The graph-node retry engine remains a different concern.
* Recheck TrackerPort's live callers, remove unused/no-op require_* probes, and split interfaces by actual consumer needs. Do not add a protocol merely because a class can be split. Issue-key/vendor parsing is adapter-owned; the resulting domain value is neutral.
* Consolidate cursor pagination beside the existing pages helper and keyed-marker lookups beside the existing domain helper, including the prefix case. Verify termination, cursor handling and existing marker selection behavior.
* Retain the original DTO/SDK-boundary findings in this issue's scope; distinguish a confirmed implementation change from a still-unverified candidate.

**Verification:** Tests must exercise behavior at adapter/consumer boundaries: transient versus permanent failures, exhaustion/cancellation, pagination completion and marker identity. Report before/after call sites and the branch/sha; no literal-ban tests or configurable backoff base is required just to remove duplication.

**FastAPI / hexagonal application of finding 1:** WorkflowRequest is an HTTP DTO and must map to the domain submission command at the HTTP boundary; tracker dispatch constructs the same domain command directly. While removing that leakage, replace repeated request.app.state lookups and per-route dependency construction with small typed Annotated/Depends providers where shared, using FastAPI dependency overrides in focused route tests. Keep Depends and Request out of application services and domain ports; do not add a DI container. Preserve JSON response contracts, streaming/SSE behavior, queue/error status codes and cancellation. Existing FastAPI lifespan stays the lifecycle entry point; its cleanup work is separately tracked under <issue id="a35bb59e-e287-4baa-9ddf-0cc099bfd07c" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-744/v03-architecture-simplification-plan-typed-privacy-focused-settings">KOD-744</issue>. [FastAPI dependencies](<https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/dependencies/>).

**JSON response boundary:** /fire and job-status routes currently manually dump Pydantic values to JSONResponse without declared success response models (api/v1/endpoints/agent.py:108–136 and [jobs.py:29](<http://jobs.py:29>)–40 at 2d4ff63). Use declared success response models and document error responses so the HTTP contract and runtime validation agree; preserve field aliases, status codes and error bodies. SSE remains an explicit streaming response. Test representative route behavior using dependency overrides; avoid introducing a duplicate domain model hierarchy solely for stylistic symmetry.

**User clarification · 2026-09-08 — reuse and extend schemas, with meaningful validation:** The HTTP dependency refactor must preserve and strengthen the existing Pydantic contracts. Prefer reusing/extending the existing job acceptance response and SSE event schemas (or sharing their field definitions where inheritance would create a false relationship) over positional primitive tuples or duplicate unconstrained models. A typing annotation/Depends alias alone is not validation.

Confirmed at PR #103 `f1ae6ac`: `api/v1/endpoints/agent.py:25` still returns `tuple[str, str]` from manually repeated route paths; `FireAcceptedResponse` and `JobAcceptedEvent` independently declare unconstrained identifiers, queue position and links. A direct probe constructs BOTH with empty job/lane values, position 0, an arbitrary non-URL status string and an empty stream link. The tuple existed on main `4661a24`; replacing AppConfig with its one consumed prefix narrows coupling and is not evidence of a newly introduced regression. The missing validation/reuse remains an acceptance gap.

**Do / Check:** Reuse/extend the existing schemas to give shared acceptance fields one validation definition, retain named status/stream fields through construction, and enforce actual invariants (nonempty handles/lane, positive accepted queue position, supported link shape). Derive job links from the registered routes with the framework's reverse lookup where suitable, so path/prefix changes do not drift from endpoints. Preserve camelCase aliases, flat JSON/SSE shapes, documented status/error behavior, dependency overrides and the current relative-link contract, including supported deployment prefixes/mounts. Verify both JSON and SSE reject malformed shared fields and emit links resolving to the registered status/stream routes. Use field-local Pydantic constraints and existing framework facilities; no parallel schema framework, no deep inheritance hierarchy, no validator on every internal call. `HttpUrl` rejects the current relative paths under the locked version, so do not impose it without an intentional API-contract change.
